description: Questions Coach Gideon asks before building or changing a program.

tags.Well supported: Consistent findings across reviews or a position stand.
tags.Moderate: Supported, but limited by study size, population or design.
tags.Standard practice: Widely used convention without strong direct evidence.
tags.Contested: Published evidence disagrees or is thin; Gideon should say so.
tags.Library design: A deliberate choice in how these plans are built.
tags.Definition: Plain-language meaning of a term used in the app.

S1.title: ACSM Position Stand: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults (2026)
S1.note: Read through a mirror PDF, about the first 100,000 of 122,000 characters.

S2.title: The Resistance Training Dose-Response: Meta-Regressions on Weekly Volume and Frequency (Sports Medicine, 2025)
S2.note: 67 studies, 79% male, mostly young adults, about 10 weeks.

S3.title: Gaining more from doing less? One-week deload during supervised resistance training (PeerJ, 2024)
S3.note: 39 trained adults; tested a full week off, not reduced volume.

S4.title: Much Ado About Zone 2 (Sports Medicine, 2025)
S4.note: Narrative review; few trials prescribed Zone 2 directly.

S5.title: Concurrent strength and endurance training: systematic review and meta-analysis (Sports Medicine, 2023)

S6.title: Factors influencing the accuracy of the repetition in reserve scale in resistance training: a systematic review (Russo et al., 2025)
S6.note: Abstract and headings only were read.

S7.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
S7.note: Excerpt did not give the muscle-strengthening frequency.

S8.title: Stretching in healthy athletes: systematic scoping review and evidence gap map (Sports Medicine, 2024)
S8.note: Evidence map of 300 trials, not a pooled analysis.

S9.title: ACE: Nutrition Scope of Practice, What You Can Do as a Personal Trainer

S10.title: NSCA-Certified Personal Trainer exam description
S10.note: Domain weights: consultation and assessment 23%, program planning 29%, program execution 36%, safety and legal 12%.

S11.title: Menstrual cycle phase does not influence training-induced hypertrophy or strength: randomized controlled trial (Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise)
S11.note: Title and search listing only; full text not read.

S12.title: Current evidence shows no influence of women's menstrual cycle phase on acute strength performance or adaptations to resistance exercise training
S12.note: Title and search listing only; full text not read.

items.question: What is your main goal: strength, size, fitness, fat loss, or sport?
items.ifAnswer: Strength: Forged or Rooted. Size: Built or Sculpted. Fitness or fat loss: Engine or Pulse for conditioning, plus lifting. Sport or power: Warrior or Valkyrie (intermediate). Never promise a fat-loss outcome; describe the training only.

items.question: How long have you trained consistently?
items.ifAnswer: Under 6 months: beginner. 6 to 24 months: intermediate. Over 2 years with steady progress: advanced. Beginners start on Forged or Rooted with easier versions.

items.question: How many days a week can you train, and for how long?
items.why: Fits the plan to the schedule.
items.ifAnswer: 3 days: run the 3 core days. 4 days: add the optional day. Under 30 minutes: use the short-session recipe (R-02). Fewer than 3 days: train what you can and say so honestly.

items.question: What equipment do you have?
items.why: Chooses the setup so every movement resolves.
items.ifAnswer: Full Gym, Home Gym (Barbell + Dumbbells), Dumbbells Only, or Bodyweight Only. The same plan works in each.

items.question: Which weekday do you want as your rest day?
items.why: The rest day anchors the week.
items.ifAnswer: Plan day 1 is the day after the chosen rest day.

items.question: Are you dealing with any injury, pain or condition a doctor has mentioned?
items.ifAnswer: Do not diagnose or rate the injury. Offer the app's general alternates and suggest clearance or guidance from a clinician before continuing. Redirect using B-04.

items.question: Do you ever get chest pain, dizziness or fainting during exercise?
items.ifAnswer: Stop and recommend medical care before training. Use the stop rules. Do not continue building a program in the same message.

items.question: Have you had a recent surgery, or are you recovering from a medical event?
items.ifAnswer: Recommend clearance from their clinician before starting. Redirect using B-04.

items.question: Do you take medication that you have been told affects exercise?
items.ifAnswer: Do not comment on medication. Suggest they ask their prescriber or pharmacist. Redirect using B-05.

items.question: Are you new to the gym, or confident with the main lifts?
items.why: Decides how much teaching to include.
items.ifAnswer: New: lean on Progressions easier versions, the how-to text and short cues. Confident: standard versions.

items.question: Is there anything you want to avoid or cannot do?
items.ifAnswer: Use the app's alternates and Progressions; do not push through a movement the user wants to avoid.

items.question: Are you pregnant, recently postpartum, or do you have pelvic floor symptoms (leaking, pressure, heaviness)?
items.ifAnswer: Do not prescribe. Suggest talking with their doctor or a pelvic health clinician before starting or changing a program. Core holds in recovery days have lower-pressure options; stop if symptoms appear. Redirect using B-07.

items.question: Do cycle symptoms (cramps, low energy) affect your training some weeks?
items.ifAnswer: Offer the low-energy-day option and scale effort by feel. Do not program by cycle phase (P-016).

note: Boundary rows must trigger the redirect text in coach-boundaries.json and never lead to diagnosis or clearance.
